digest.component_or_area: ADR (Architecture Decision Record) indexing and collision resolution
propositions: ADR numbering collisions exist: 91 ADR files map to only 69 distinct numbers, with 17 numbers reused across 22 files (e.g., five unrelated ADRs numbered 0037)
Collisions arise from stale-base merges (16 of 22 cases) where authors did not refetch after an earlier ADR landed with the same number; pre-merge CI checks cannot prevent this due to rebase races
The solution is a per-number marker file `docs/adr/.numbers/NNNN` whose content is the ADR filename; two ADRs claiming the same number produce an add/add conflict that Gerrit cannot auto-resolve
Remediation assigns the number to the earliest-landed ADR in each collision group and renumbers the 22 later ADRs to 0070-0091 in ascending landing-date order

CI check and index generation (scripts/check_adr_numbers.py, scripts/gen_adr_index.py) enforce marker-to-ADR bijection, unique numbers, and referential integrity: all slug-bearing cross-references in docs/ and src/ are rewritten to final ADR numbers, with resolution tier recorded in RENUMBERING.md

Bare ADR number citations in commit history (e.g., CONTRIBUTING.md:173) that cannot be mechanically disambiguated are recorded UNRESOLVED in RENUMBERING.md; the single immutable history reference is handled this way by design
